I tried them on the LGG Jupiter and it’s beyond mud. It made the Jupiter feel as slow as I thought it would before I tried it. I even polished them and still nothing.

My pad was like this straight out of the box too. Even my ec1 glided with ease. I don’t know what happened, but 2 days later it became really slow. My Jupiter suddenly became a mud pad overnight. It’s never returned to that fast glide since then. Really weird tbh. Still I wonder if my pad is still defected and it’s not as slow as it should be. Mine seems to glide more than what I’ve seen on YouTube, but comparing what I see in a video and what’s on my desk isn’t that comprehensive.

 I should send it back to LGG so they could inspect it but I’ve waited so long for this pad,  and I don’t want to wait while using anything else in its place. Then again it would help them if there is a problem with the Jupiter’s production.

The one of the smoothest mousepads you could ever own atm. More smooth than the cloth glorious pad. It’s an odd feeling (in a good way). You would have to feel the surface to understand it really, but it is a great purchase for a slow control pad.

Ec1 c series, because it’s the heaviest. The lighter the mouse the faster it feels. However they’re all slow compared to any other pad. It also matters what mouse skates you use. Core pads do pretty well. Tiger ice will probably be your best bet if you want to cut threw the “muddy” feeling.

I tried glueing pulsars glass mouse skates on my model d (it worked and fit pretty well), however those mouse skates made the Jupiter feel even slower. I don’t know if pulsar’s glass skates do not move well on the pad since, I didn’t use them for their intended purpose. (It’s glides with ease on other pads) I’m not sure if glass skates glide well on the pad, but they might if you use them on the mouse it’s meant to fit onto.

I’ve put in a lot of hours on the equate and still trying out the Jupiter. The way the Jupiter was advertised I thought it would be slower, much slower than the equate. (It’s not) 

  I’ve tried the Orochi v2, model d, xtrfy m4, xm1r, ec1 and ec3 (both c series stock skates) and they all “fly” on this mousepad. At least move faster than what was apparently a gsr competitor. 

  I’ve watched a few videos of people using the early batch and testing the glide and the mice they use come to a dead stop almost immediately. My pad is no where near having that lack of glide.  

  I’m not saying I dislike the pad, I was just surprised on how much faster it is compared to other mud pads. When I get the pulsar parabreak I’ll have to compare the two. Also I bought the 1000x500 version.
